collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager said yes too quickly to leading the fishing crew: take it back, or keep the yes.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) was asked this morning whether (subject.he/she) wanted to lead the fishing crew next season, and (subject.he/she) said yes straight away, before (subject.he/she) even thought about it. Now, at lunch, (subject.he/she) is thinking about it. Early mornings. Organizing people. Being the one who's blamed when the fish don't come. (subject.He/she) goes to find (friend), who asked (subject.him/her).

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "I said yes too fast," says (subject). "I'm sorry. Can I say no instead?" (friend) blinks. Then shrugs. "Of course. Better now than in the middle of the season." (subject) walks away feeling lighter. A year later, (subject.he/she) asks if the job is still open. It isn't. (subject.He/she) is fine with that too.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) opens (subject.his/her) mouth to take it back, then hesitates. "Actually," (subject.he/she) says, "I'm nervous. But I think I want it." (friend) nods. "Being nervous is fair." The season comes. Some days are hard. Some days the fish come and (subject) is the one everyone cheers. (subject.He/she) never decides for sure if the yes was right. (subject.He/she) just keeps doing it.
